# Dimension Reduction

Dimension reduction (DR) is the process of summarizing data with lots of dimensions. We need this because it is often cumbersome or nearly impossible to work with high-dimensional data.

::: callout-tip
Usually, we refer to variables as dimensions.
:::

**Questions**:

1.  What's one way of visualizating relationships between 2 variables?
2.  How many relationships are there if we have $n$ variables?
3.  Can we think of some examples of dimension reduction?

# Tweet Example

## Preprocessing

First, we will start with what we did last time:

```{r}
## Load data
data_path <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cardiffnlp/tweeteval/refs/heads/main/datasets/emotion/test_text.txt"
labels_path <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cardiffnlp/tweeteval/refs/heads/main/datasets/emotion/test_labels.txt"
  
tweets <- read_delim(data_path, delim = "\t", col_names = F)
labels <- read_delim(labels_path, delim = "\t", col_names = F)

# Combine Datasets
tweets <- tweets |>
  rename(text = X1) |>
  bind_cols(labels) |>
  rename(label = X1) |>
  mutate(ID = 1:nrow(tweets))

# Tokenize
tweets_token <- tweets |>
  unnest_tokens(word, text)

## TF-IDF
tf_idf <- tweets_token |>
  count(word, ID) |>
  bind_tf_idf(word, ID, n)
```
